course_name_original: Russian B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
course_name_en: Russian B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
prerequisites: Russian language proficiency at least A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write understandable informational and argumentative texts on general and industry topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present their conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.
Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Can use grammatical constructions, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic, and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Noun: accusative plural of animate nouns, neuter nouns ending in -мя, like время (revision), acronyms like турпоход, шоп-тур
Adjective: comparative degree, superlative degree with suffixes -eйш-, -aйш- and with prefix най-, short form as predicate
Pronoun: negative with particles ни, не(-), like ничего, нечего, indefinite with particles -то, -нибудь like кто-то, кто-нибудь

Verb: perfective, imperfective verbs (e.g., лететь - летать), imperative mood for 3rd person singular and plural and for 1st person plural, verbs of motion (куда? +B.) and state (где? + Msc.), adverbial and adjectival participles (active and passive), passive voice
Sentence constructions: cardinal number 2, 3, 4 + adjective + masculine or neuter noun
Translational attempts
University, studies, student life (Вуз, учёба, студенческая жизнь) - Education in Poland and Russia, university choice - Description of the faculty and nature of studies
Future plans, career choice (Планы на будущее, выбор профессии) - Applying for a job - Ways for students to earn money
Vanishing and most prestigious professions (Исчезающие и престижные профессии) - Naming professions and describing professional activities
Job interview (Собеседование) - Ability to present oneself during a job interview, dress code
Job offers in the press or on the Internet (Оферты работы, объявления) - Creating job advertisements, employment agency
Examples of formal letters, e.g., application, complaint, cover letter (Коммерческая корреспонденция) - Writing various forms of formal letters; business correspondence
Office equipment and supplies (Оргтехника) - Ordering office supplies, names of office equipment
Passport and visa formalities (Оформление визы) - Asking questions, providing information, writing invitations
Filling out forms, e.g., customs declaration (Как заполнить таможенную декларацию) - Types of customs and visa forms, blanks
Booking a hotel room (Бронировка номера в отеле) - Ability to book accommodation, tickets, etc.
At the station, at the airport (Ha вокзалe, в аэропортy) - Most important places, e.g., waiting room, terminal, timetable; activities related to travel
Sport and tourism (Спорт и туризм) - Sports disciplines, pros and cons of playing sports - Sporting events and facilities
Health status, doctor (Врач, болезнь) - Treatment, first aid - Medical specialties, medical supplies, etc.
Environment we live in (Окружающая среda) - Ecological threats and environmental protection - Pro-ecological behaviors
Us and culture (Мы и культурa) - Cultural events - Film, music, museum
Technology around us, Internet (Техника вокруг нас, Интернет) - Inventions, electronic devices, computer - Role of the Internet, etiquette rules on the Internet
Holidays and celebrations in Poland and Russia (Государственные и церковные праздники) - Holiday attributes, giving wishes
Conducting a discussion – Проведение дискуссии
Commenting on information – Комментарии
Conducting conversations about everyday situations – Разговоры на бытовые темы
Giving advice – Советы
Expressing wishes – Желания
Forecasting – Прогнозирование
Stating reasons – Представление причин
Resolving conflicts, reacting in conflict situations.
Conducting conversations about rules of conduct.
Conducting short conversations with casually met people.
Justifying one's position, citing arguments "for" and "against", constructive criticism.
Preparing and conducting a job interview.
Filling out forms.
Drafting various types of texts: emails and private and official letters, e.g., cover letter, CV, letters to the editor, complaints, applications.
Listening comprehension of interviews, conversations of general content, as well as popular science statements.
Reading comprehension of popular science texts.
Delivering a presentation related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: The condition for passing is to receive a positive grade from all colloquia conducted during the semester. If a negative grade is received, the student has the right to improve the grade according to the following rules: improving a negative grade obtained in the first attempt results in cancelling the negative grade and replacing it with a positive grade, which will count towards the average. Improving a grade obtained in the second attempt results in entering the average of the two received grades into the record sheet; the average partial grade for passing the test cannot be less than 3.0. Unjustified absence from a test results in losing the attempt. Each student has the right to two retake colloquia, which can take place at intervals of not less than 2 days. The student has the right to see their graded work and ask for an explanation of the grading method and correct answers, but is not allowed to photograph or otherwise copy test materials. The student is obliged to have the language textbook and complete homework; failure to have the required materials (textbook, homework) results in an annotation of "unprepared" in the record sheet, and the instructor may refuse to pass a student who was unprepared for more than 1/2 of the classes, even if they passed all colloquia. Additional grades are given for activity in class, optional homework, presentations, and other activities benefiting their group. The condition for admission to the exam is passing the compulsory language course semesters. The final grade for the language course is determined as the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained by the student from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. In case of justified absence due to illness, the student must provide a medical certificate no later than 14 days after the justified absence. In case of unjustified absence, the student should contact the instructor, who will individually provide a way to make up for the absence within 14 days from the date of absence. Unjustified absence from two classes does not require making up. If the number of unjustified absences exceeds 7, the instructor should refuse to pass the semester, even if some of them were previously made up.
